entities.summary:
The 2023-2024 mpox epidemic was a global outbreak of the monkeypox virus that began in Africa in September 2023, spreading rapidly across the world. This epidemic was a significant public health event, causing widespread illness and death, and highlighting the need for increased global cooperation in responding to infectious disease outbreaks.

The mpox epidemic was a complex and multifaceted event, with various factors contributing to its spread. The virus was initially identified in Africa, but it quickly spread to other parts of the world, including Europe, North America, and South America. The epidemic was characterized by a high number of cases, particularly among men who have sex with men, and a high mortality rate.

The mpox epidemic had significant consequences for public health, global health security, and international relations. It led to increased investment in global health infrastructure, improved surveillance and response capabilities, and a greater recognition of the need for global cooperation in responding to infectious disease outbreaks.

One of the most striking aspects of the mpox epidemic was its impact on the LGBTQ+ community. The virus disproportionately affected men who have sex with men, highlighting the need for greater support and resources for this community.

The mpox epidemic was a major public health event that highlighted the importance of global cooperation, improved surveillance and response capabilities, and increased investment in global health infrastructure.
